corrections.form_value: Only S1: 12-week quasi-experiment (heritage design course); computational ablation omitted.
corrections.source_says: Add a separate model_only study for the computational ablation comparing a LoRA network trained on uncorrected archaeological images with one trained on images calibrated by RestoreFormer++. The evaluation used 500 generated outputs from each model, not people; participant counts should remain null. The restored model had an FID score reduced by approximately 16.4, 95% CI [-18.20, -14.60], and a CLIP semantic alignment score increased by 0.07, 95% CI [0.064, 0.076]. This model-only study does not constitute randomized AI assistance to people and does not enter the core dataset.
corrections.quote: Evaluating a random sample of 500 generative outputs from each, the ablation revealed a substantial performance divergence.
corrections.locator: p. 4, Dataset provenance, curation, and annotation protocol, computational ablation paragraph

confirmed: Read the entire 420-line markdown conversion, including Appendix A, references, and declarations, and checked the relevant PDF pages directly; the PDF contains 12 pages (pp. 1-12).

The source is the published Scientific Reports (2026) 16:29360 article by Tingting Yu and Yixin Li, DOI 10.1038/s41598-026-71408-2; the document title matches the form (p. 1). Received 9 March 2026 and accepted 9 September 2026 (p. 10); published online 19 September 2026, verified from the embedded date image (p. 11). The open-access license is on p. 12.

The people study is explicitly quasi-experimental and assigns intact class sections to two groups without stating random allocation. The form's quasi_people design, observational context, and core = no are supported; no randomized people study is reported anywhere in this source (p. 3, Methodology; pp. 1-12, including Appendix A).

The final sample is 118 people, with 59 in each group, not a count of artifacts or ratings; the sample exceeds the 50-person threshold. The paper reports 68 females, 50 males, mean age 20.4 and SD 1.1. People randomized and the number excluded are not reported, so the null randomized counts are appropriate (p. 3, Methodology).

The stated exclusions are prior systematic diffusion-model training or incomplete attendance records; the source gives no number removed. Table 2 reports degrees of freedom (1, 116), as noted in the form (p. 3, Methodology; p. 6, Table 2).

Participants were second-year undergraduate design students; the intervention lasted 12 weeks between September and December 2025. The control curriculum used manual sketching, Adobe Illustrator, Rhino, and physical prototyping, while the experimental group used the customized generative pipeline (p. 3, Methodology; Chinese institutional affiliations on p. 1).

The pipeline used Stable Diffusion v1.5, Kohya_ss LoRA fine-tuning, and ControlNet; the heritage datasets contained 1,500 Xiang Embroidery images and 2,000 Changsha Kiln images, with Qwen-VL tagging. Students used the pipeline from ideation through final rendering (pp. 3-4, Methodology and Dataset provenance).

Each student submitted a final design portfolio containing their heritage artifact. Three blinded independent experts scored Cultural Authenticity, Design Innovation, and Technical Feasibility on a 1-to-100 rubric; ICCs were 0.89, 0.93, and 0.84, respectively. These are output-scored outcomes, not self-reports (p. 5, artifact evaluation paragraph).
S1-O1 Design Innovation: Control mean (SD) 68.9 (9.6), Experimental 87.9 (6.6), t = 12.57, p < 0.001. Every value in the reported string matches its cited table (p. 8, Table 3).
S1-O2 Cultural Authenticity: Control mean (SD) 72.4 (8.2), Experimental 86.7 (6.4), t = 10.61, p < 0.001. Every value in the reported string matches its cited table (p. 8, Table 3).
S1-O3 Technical Feasibility: Control mean (SD) 76.5 (7.9), Experimental 81.4 (8.0), t = 3.34, p = 0.001. Every value in the reported string matches its cited table (p. 8, Table 3).

The one-line finding correctly reports the 12-week, 118-person quasi-experiment and the higher Experimental Group scores, with all of its numerical outcome claims matching Table 3 (p. 3, Methodology; p. 8, Table 3).

Aesthetic Appreciation, Aesthetic Implementation, and Cultural Identity were assessed with 7-point agreement scales at Week 1 and Week 12; they are distinct from the expert-scored artifact outcomes and do not establish output-scored creativity (p. 4, psychometric assessment paragraph; p. 6, Tables 1-2).

An external supplementary R script is named, and the paper links supplementary material through its DOI; Appendix A is included in the main PDF and describes the inference workflow rather than another people experiment (p. 10, Data availability and Appendix A; p. 12, Additional information).

This is primary empirical research rather than a synthesis, so the synthesis counts and pooled estimates appropriately remain empty. Figure 2 displays expert-score distributions, not a scored across-person diversity outcome; no after-AI-removal outcome is reported (pp. 3-8, Methodology and Analysis; p. 8, Figure 2).
summary: The nonrandomized classification, 118-person final sample, and all Table 3 statistics in the reported strings and one-line finding are confirmed. Corrections concern an unsupported count of class sections, the omitted model-only ablation, an overbroad supplement description, the missing code URL, and unflagged discrepancies between Table 3 and Figure 2.
